description: REQ-004's edge case explicitly requires: 'Missing details.currencyIn/currencyOut fields entirely: refuse (cannot verify economics).' The pure function evaluate_relay_fee() correctly fails closed when given None, but the orchestration layer never lets it see None -- it silently substitutes the LOCALLY-COMPUTED requested amount instead of the relay-reported input value whenever the field is absent, then feeds that fabricated number into the fee-cap check. Concretely: if a relay quote returns details={'currencyOut': {'amountUsd': '6.45'}} with no currencyIn key at all, in_usd resolves to the local `amount` (e.g. 6.50) via the `or amount` fallback instead of None, and evaluate_relay_fee(in_usd=6.50, out_usd=6.45) computes a passing 0.77% fee -- even though the quote's actual input-side economics were never reported by relay at all. This defeats the fail-closed guarantee of the pure function precisely in the failure mode REQ-004 names, and does so for the paramount money-safety cap in this feature (the 8% relay-fee cap). No orchestration test (tests/test_franklin_sol_base_refill.py) ever supplies a quote fixture missing currencyIn/currencyOut -- every relay_quote fixture in the suite includes both fields fully populated, so this fallback path is never exercised or caught by the 57 new tests.

evidence.snippet:
in_usd = float((details.get("currencyIn") or {}).get("amountUsd") or amount)
out_usd = float((details.get("currencyOut") or {}).get("amountUsd") or 0)
fee_decision = evaluate_relay_fee(in_usd=in_usd, out_usd=out_usd)
